name: Wisconsin
agency: Wisconsin Department of Transportation (WisDOT), Division of Motor Vehicles

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, 10 of them at night (WisDOT; permits issued before July 11, 2021: 30 hours with 10 at night)
teen.holdPermit: 6 months, violation free for those 6 months (WisDOT)
teen.nightLimit: Probationary under 18, first 9 months: midnight to 5 a.m. alone only between home, school and work (secondary sources)
teen.passengerLimit: Probationary under 18: any number of immediate family members and one other person (WisDOT)
teen.phone: Instruction permit and probationary license: no phone at all, hand-held or hands-free, except to report an emergency (2011 Wisconsin Act 164, since Nov. 1, 2012); forfeiture $20 to $40 first offense

bac.under21: absolute sobriety: any amount (Wis. Stat. 346.63(2m)); 3-month suspension, $200 forfeiture, 4 points

notes: Permit age left null: sources conflict. A search snippet attributed to WisDOT says minimum age 15 (since July 2021, with driver education enrollment); many secondary sites say 15 and a half.
Separate road signs test: 15 questions, 12 correct (secondary). Knowledge test 50 questions, 40 correct (secondary).

Supervisor with a permit holder: licensed adult at least 21 with at least 2 years of driving experience, or instructor or parent (secondary). One secondary source says night driving needs a supervisor 25 or older; not used.
Probationary license: at least 16, approved driver education, adult sponsor (WisDOT).
Move Over (Wis. Stat. 346.072): leave the lane closest to the stopped vehicle or slow down; 2025 Wisconsin Act 54 added disabled vehicles; fine up to $300.
First OWI offense is a civil violation, not a crime (WisDOT, Wisconsin Watch).
Speed: freeways 65 mph, 70 mph where posted since 2015 Wisconsin Act 19; 15 mph passing a school when children are present (Wis. Stat. 346.57(4)(a)).
School bus 20-foot stopping distance and divided-highway rule were found only in an unclear source; not used.

English handbook: a search listing pointed to a file named BDS126 Motorists Handbook under wisconsindot.gov/Documents/dmv/shared/, exact URL not confirmed. The Spanish manual page is official; WisDOT calls it a condensed version.
Official wisconsindot.gov pages could not be read (fetch blocked); facts come from search snippets.
